mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline returns during periods of FEDFUNDS decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline returns during periods of UNRATE increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over the last two months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline returns during periods of HOUST increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline returns during periods of INDPRO decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the last month, it signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline returns during periods of joint RSAFS increase and UNRATE decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% within the last month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline returns during periods of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 within the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline returns during periods of PAYEMS increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 0.5% within the last quarter, it signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% and INDPRO decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline returns during periods of low GDPC1 growth and decreasing INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).
